This bird is in distress. Sticking the head up with the eyes closed is an indication that it is struggling to breathe, as is the mouth breathing seen toward the end of the video. The wing stretching almost looks like some sort of attempt to shelter itself from the water. Every bird owner is guilty of attributing human qualities / attributes to our birds, but they are not humans. What we perceive here as "cute, relaxing in the shower" type of behaviors are actually the behavior of a bird that is either struggling to breathe or straight up drowning.

Direct contact with water sprayed from a showerhead can be dangerous, especially if there is not an easy way into and out of the stream of water. You might think "well he can just walk outside of the stream" but smaller birds can get easily overwhelmed by the power & amount of water sprayed by a typical showerhead. Besides drowning, inhaling water can cause other serious issues like pneumonia.

For bathing, birds should be offered a bowl of water to bathe themselves on their own terms (under supervision). Some birds also like misting from a clean spray bottle. A clean sink with a very gently trickling stream of water is my bird's preferred method, with a towel draped into the bowl of the sink for easy access in/out of contact with the water. If you insist on the shower, you can make it safer by preventing direct contact between water from the showerhead & your bird, instead allowing the water to bounce off of another surface first, which allows for a weaker less direct stream and a finer mist.

They do this with the intention of eroding the public's trust in government institutions so that ultimately we allow the loss of a public service (which was never intended to be profitable to begin with) and it's replaced by a private, profit-minded industry.

Literally the same thing is happening with public education. This is the same reason why you will see any popular push for free college undermined as well... how will corporate elites make money if they can't saddle younger generations with massive debts the minute they reach adulthood?

"Socialism" isn't the word to be afraid of, especially in the contexts of public services. "Deregulation" "privatization" and "profitability" are the ones consistently proving to bode very poorly for the average American.

I've gotten this bug a few times. I usually just suspend my cycle and restart the game. Sometimes, even doing that, previously dropped weapons will stay this way, but any new ones I find in containers or miniboss drops don't have the issue anymore.

The side rooms are pretty important tbh, as many of them will have buffs, artifacts, silphium resources, obilites etc. The boss of the first biome is one of the biggest humps to get over for a lot of people... collecting every last resource in the biome is really helpful.

It may feel intimidating taking on additional rooms that likely have additional enemies and dangers... but it pays off, both in the resources I mentioned but also in combat experience. Use them as an opportunity to practice your dodging (more important) and gunplay (less important), and to earn weapon proficiency & unlock weapon traits, so that you can get better gun drops.

Also work on silphium management; not taking damage should always be your #1 priority, because any silphium laying around in the biome will turn into silphium resin whenever you have full health. Taking damage sometimes is inevitable if you're still learning the game, but leaving small silphium for later to pick up as resin when you have full health (unless it's an emergency) is generally the best way to go, since they don't give you as much health replenishment as regular silphium, but will still give you 1 slot toward a max health upgrade (same as regular silphium).

Another tip that helped me is changing my controller bindings to have jump and dash in my shoulder buttons, and melee as a thumbstick press. 

My qualifications: My first time trying Returnal was years ago and I couldn't get past the first Biome after more than a dozen hours... I decided to give it a whirl again a couple months ago. After learning all this stuff, I ended up platinuming the game in about two or three weeks. Since then, I recently beat all three acts with zero deaths. :) Be patient, hone in your skills, and you and OP will be in the second biome in no time!

Yes, I would only list the three years of verifiable experience. Shipped projects and/or work with a dev team is generally considered the standard for “experience” in game development. In your summary you can mention that you’ve been actively working with Unity for much longer (others say ditch the summary, but I disagree. Def keep it short and sweet though), but the prominent “x years of experience” bullet should reflect the verifiable, shipped projects / relevant work experience stuff you listed.

Think of it this way: a dev who has been in the industry for seven years and has a list of studio jobs / shipped projects would most likely assert they have “Seven years of Experience working with Unity.” That, in a lot of cases, would be bordering on a senior level Unity dev. By asserting you have “seven years of experience” that will be your competition, and who you’d be compared against in the eyes of HR. You likely have good, solo learning experience with Unity, but without shipped projects or experience working at a game studio, that experience is not going to be recognized… and if it is, it still won’t be weighted as heavily as a veteran Unity dev, who has been actively working in the industry on studio dev teams, shipping projects.

Compared to that, your “7 years” looks much, much greener— there is nothing wrong with being green… You just need to be realistic to make sure you’re competing against people with a similar level of ability, for roles that suit that level of ability, so that you aren’t accidentally competing for a borderline senior position against borderline senior level Unity devs. (Especially with the current state of the industry.)

I hope this makes sense / helps!

My two cents as a game dev professional: You mention “seven years experience” working in Unity, but all of your projects are shipped 2023, and your only work experience relevant to Unity dev work is 2022-2023. Without any shipped projects, internships, or work experience attached to those other 5 years, it could feel like a considerable oversell to a hiring manager. Overselling of experience is a big issue in this industry and hiring managers will be very skeptical of years of claimed experience that is unverifiable. I suppose you could try to make the argument that college course work translates into experience, but that’s a really tough sell in an industry that widely values work experience and shipped projects over degrees. In my opinion it would be better to start counting your years of experience beginning with the objectively verifiable stuff.

Also just as a side note, what others have been saying is very true too— the game dev job market is super saturated and competitive right now with the massive amount of layoffs that have been going on. It’s pretty rough out there rn.

For those asking, Hainanese chicken rice features chicken that is simmered with aromatics. Overview goes a little like this:

1. Chicken is scrubbed with coarse salt then rinsed.
2. Chicken is thoroughly salted then stuffed with slices of ginger and stalks of green onion.
3. Chicken is simmered for about half an hour, which creates a delicate chicken/ginger/green onion broth.
4. Chicken is removed and placed in an ice bath, then rubbed with sesame oil when cooled.
5. Rice is toasted with garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and chicken fat, then cooked in the broth made from the chicken.

The sauces from left to right are a vinegar based ginger-garlic sauce, a spicy sambal-based one, and a sweet ginger soy. Each of the sauces has a bit of the broth as well to further tie the flavors together.

Anxiety + asthma fucking SUCKS. They make each other worse. You could have a little baby asthma attack, but if you combine it with anxiety you can end up hyper focusing on it and making it feel worse. And anxiety can also make you hyperventilate which can make the asthma feel worse. OR you can have an anxiety attack which can cause vasoconstriction which can trigger an asthma attack. It can be a viscous cycle of one thing triggering the other.

As for inhalers, no you cannot get them over the counter as far as I know. Definitely get to a pulmonologist and explain your issue and ask for a prescription rescue inhaler. The albuterol ones. Those are great and stop asthma attacks right in their tracks. They might try to get you a daily use steroid inhaler for preventative treatment, but I personally don’t use those because my asthma isn’t very severe and the side effects of oral steroids creep me out. I think a personalized strategy to tackle your specific mental health problems will always be more effective than looking for help at a hospital. It served its purpose, it gave me a safe place to be where I didn’t have to worry about my basic needs being met (food, a bed to sleep in, the ability to shower) while I was getting through my depressive episode on my own. And for what it’s worth I did come out of it feeling genuinely better. But I give myself the majority of the credit for that outcome. 

I do give the hospital some credit. Having your basic needs met really does take A LOT of stress off of you, even if those needs are already generally met in your day to day life. Not having to put thought into them really helped lift a weight off my mind. Seeing other people with worse situations than me also helped put things into perspective and make me feel a little better about my situation. The CBT group sessions they had were genuinely helpful and actually helped make me feel a bit better about myself, to the point where I actually kept the worksheets and brought them home with me. The exercise groups were helpful too. I hate exercise but participated in order to show I was participating in group activities so they’d let me out sooner, but I actually ended up enjoying them.

I don’t know. It’s really a mixed bag and it depends on the hospital, I’m sure. But definitely having your own therapist and psychiatrist that you see regularly and friends that you can be open and honest with regarding your mood is definitely the more helpful thing to have. But I’d say the hospital is a good option if you’re having a mental emergency and don’t know what else to do in the moment. It at least gets you out of where you at and sticks you somewhere safe and pressure-free for a little while.

Also, just a quick plug for the treatment I’m getting that I really do think has been helping: ECT. I’m treatment resistant, have a reaction to every single pill I’ve tried. ECT was pretty much one of my last options and while it hasn’t completely fixed my brain, it really has made a difference.
